rounds.text: The market has heavily punished the stock, leaving it sitting at a mere 7 percent of the way up its 52-week range [E5]. However, this extreme markdown has compressed the valuation to a price-to-book ratio of just 0.64x, with the price at ₹ 23.0 against a book value of ₹ 36.0 [E2], meaning investors are acquiring the underlying assets at a steep discount to their stated value. Beneath this depressed sentiment, operational green shoots are already forming as evidenced by sales rising quarter-over-quarter [E54]. Furthermore, earnings growth is actively accelerating [E55], signalling an inflection point that the trailing metrics fail to capture. Conceded: [E1], [E4], [E6], [E7], [E8], [E11], [E12], [E13], [E43], [E48], [E58], [E63].

The bull attempts to frame the 7 percent position in the 52-week range [E5] and the 0.64x price-to-book ratio [E2] as a deep-value discount, but this ignores the reality that capital destruction deserves a markdown rather than a multiple. Conceded: [E2] and [E5]. The reliance on sales rising quarter-over-quarter [E54] and accelerating earnings growth [E55] as an inflection point is completely contradicted by the catastrophic trailing performance of a 93 percent drop in TTM profit growth [E13] alongside a 53 percent year-over-year sales collapse [E58]. Furthermore, buying assets below book value holds zero merit when the company generates a return on equity of a negligible 0.4 percent [E7] and a return on capital employed of just 2.9 percent [E6]. Finally, celebrating green shoots cannot mask a multi-year structural decline featuring five-year profit contraction of 19 percent [E11], a three-year profit destruction of 63 percent [E12], and a negative five-year sales growth rate of 1 percent [E8].
